what: Two-sided corpus for the Spanish and Portuguese deterministic filters. ACCEPT cases must match; REJECT cases must not. Without the second half you cannot tell a working filter from an inverted one (darking, 2026-08-26).
how_reject_was_built: Every REJECT case whose `why` carries a number was found by scripts/corpus/multilang-fp-probe.ts against 441,690 Spanish and 444,028 Portuguese Tatoeba sentences, Don Quijote, and our own 56,919-post corpus. They are not invented; they are what the filter fired on.
locale_field: The reader's locale, as navigator.language reports it. null means unknown, which is the common case and gets global lists only.

coded_cases_what: Two-sided corpus for the Spanish and Portuguese rules in coded-harm-catcher.ts. These are the HIDE tier: a match hides the post or comment and the reader never learns it existed, so the REJECT half carries more weight than the ACCEPT half. Every REJECT case marked (corpus) is a sentence the rules actually fired on across 441,690 Spanish and 444,028 Portuguese Tatoeba sentences plus Don Quijote, before it was fixed.

coded_cases.why: ES; the corpus contains three real uses of this and no benign one
with the diacritic; detectCodedHarm folds before matching
PT proclitic imperative at the start of its clause
PT hyphenated enclitic, only ever an imperative
ES: explicit token plus a directed verb

l1_cases_what: Two-sided corpus for the L1 cascade (src/core/techniques/) in Spanish and Portuguese. ACCEPT cases must produce present=true for the named technique; REJECT cases must produce no present technique at all. The REJECT half also locks the ENGLISH behaviour that changed when the shared rules were narrowed: those rules were language-blind, so the Spanish and Portuguese false positives they produced were English false positives too, and no test covered them.
